name: nanodump
help: Dump LSASS or inspect its PID with NanoDump

arguments.name: dump-path
arguments.desc: Dump name or full path for file output

arguments.name: write-file
arguments.desc: Write a dump to disk (1); fileless callbacks are unsupported by Sliver

arguments.name: chunk-size
arguments.desc: Fileless output chunk size in bytes

arguments.name: valid-sig
arguments.desc: Use a valid minidump signature (1); 0 needs signature restoration

arguments.name: duplicate
arguments.desc: Duplicate an existing LSASS handle (0 or 1)

arguments.name: duplicate-elevate
arguments.desc: Duplicate and elevate an LSASS handle (0 or 1)

arguments.name: getpid
arguments.desc: Print the LSASS PID without dumping (0 or 1)

arguments.name: seclogon-local
arguments.desc: Use the local seclogon leak (0 or 1)

arguments.name: seclogon-remote
arguments.desc: Use the remote seclogon leak (0 or 1)

arguments.name: seclogon-binary
arguments.desc: Target path to a matching EXE staged before seclogon-local use

arguments.name: shtinkering
arguments.desc: Use Shtinkering (1); set write-file and valid-sig to 0

long_help: The arguments match the upstream NanoDump BOF ABI. Use --getpid 1 to print the LSASS PID without creating a dump. Standard dumps default to disk output and a valid signature. Sliver does not reconstruct NanoDump's Cobalt Strike fileless callbacks. The seclogon-local technique needs a matching NanoDump EXE staged on the target before invoking this BOF. Other modes and their prerequisites are documented in the upstream README.
